subject: GSM Phone Maintenance and Repairs
practicalPaper: There is no separate practical paper: Paper 2 Section B has two practical-work questions, both answered in 50 minutes for 40 marks. These test hands-on knowledge such as identifying tools and components, disassembly and reassembly order, fault-finding steps, measurements on the PCB and software repair procedures, alongside the essay questions in Section A.

practicals.title: Workshop safety and protection against static
practicals.aim: To set up a safe phone repair bench, use anti-static protection and identify basic safety facilities.
materials: Battery fire bag or metal container with sand
safety: Disconnect the battery before working on any board.
Never puncture or bend a lithium battery; a swollen battery must be removed and stored safely.
Keep IPA away from hot tools; it is flammable.
procedure: Ground the ESD mat and wear the wrist strap connected to it.
Arrange tools so hot tools are on stands away from cables and IPA.
Switch on the fume extractor before soldering.
Check the location of the extinguisher, first aid box and battery fire container.
Demonstrate safe handling of a phone battery.
Write the workshop rules on a chart.
practicals.expectedObservations: Bench is organised, grounded and safe; the wrist strap tester shows a good connection.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: A typical ESD wrist strap contains a 1 MΩ safety resistor. If a person touches 230 V by accident, the current through the strap is limited to 230/1 000 000 = 0.23 mA — far below dangerous levels.
precautions: Test the wrist strap regularly.
Do not wear the wrist strap when working on mains-powered equipment that is live.
sourcesOfError: Poor earth connection of the mat.
commonMistakes: Touching ICs without ESD protection.
Leaving the hot-air gun on the bench.
examTips: List safety rules and safety facilities (first aid box, fire extinguisher, ESD mat).
Explain why static damages phone ICs.

practicals.title: Identifying phone repair tools and equipment
practicals.topic: Common Tools and Equipment for Hardware and Software Repairs
practicals.aim: To identify hardware and software repair tools and state the use of each.
apparatus: Precision screwdriver set (Phillips, star/pentalobe, Torx, tri-point)
safety: Keep sharp picks and tweezers capped.
Hot tools on stands only.
procedure: Lay out each tool and write its name.
Classify as opening, holding, measuring, soldering or software tools.

Match screwdriver bits to sample phone screws.
Identify software tools: flashing software, firmware packages, drivers.
Present results in a table.
practicals.expectedObservations: Each tool is correctly named, classified and its use stated.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Using the wrong bit damages screw heads: if a phone has 12 screws and a technician strips 1 in 4 by using wrong bits, 12/4 = 3 screws will need replacement — a cost avoided by matching bits.
precautions: Use plastic tools near flex cables and batteries.
commonMistakes: Prying with metal tools near the battery.
examTips: Name tools listed in the syllabus with uses.

practicals.title: Disassembling and reassembling a mobile phone
practicals.aim: To disassemble a phone in the correct sequence, identify the parts and reassemble it in working order.
safety: Power off and disconnect the battery first.
Use gentle heat to soften adhesive; do not overheat the battery.
procedure: Switch off; remove SIM tray and back cover (heat and suction cup if glued).
Remove screws, placing each on the screw mat in position.
Disconnect the battery connector first.
Disconnect flex cables (display, charging port, cameras) with a spudger.
Remove the board; identify speakers, vibrator, microphone, buzzer, SIM socket, keypad/display.
Reassemble in reverse, reconnecting the battery last.
Test all functions.
practicals.expectedObservations: The phone works fully after reassembly; no screws left over and all flexes seated.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Screws of different lengths: a 3.0 mm screw placed where a 2.0 mm one belongs protrudes 3.0 − 2.0 = 1.0 mm and can pierce the board or display — which is why the screw map is kept.
precautions: Record screw positions.
Never pull flex cables by the cable; lift by the connector.
sourcesOfError: Hidden clips or screws under labels.
commonMistakes: Reconnecting the battery before other flexes.
Using long screws in short holes.
examTips: Write the disassembly sequence in numbered steps.
Note special maintenance needs of flip and slide phones (hinge flex).

practicals.title: Drawing the block diagram of a mobile phone
practicals.aim: To draw the block diagram of a mobile phone (power, logic/memory and radio sections) and locate each section on a real board.
safety: Handle scrap boards carefully; edges can be sharp.
procedure: Draw the power section: battery, charging IC, power management IC (PMIC).
Draw the logic/memory section: CPU, memory (RAM, flash), SIM interface, display, keypad, audio.
Draw the radio section: antenna, antenna switch, power amplifier, transceiver.
Connect blocks with arrows to show signal and power flow.
Label each block and state its function.
Locate the sections on the scrap board; shielding cans usually cover radio and CPU areas.
practicals.expectedObservations: The diagram clearly separates the power, memory/logic and radio units, matching the layout on the board.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Board area estimate: a board measuring 120 mm × 60 mm = 7 200 mm²; if the radio section occupies a 30 mm × 25 mm area, it is 750/7 200 × 100 ≈ 10% of the board.
precautions: Use a ruler for neat blocks and arrows.
sourcesOfError: Different phone models arrange sections differently.
commonMistakes: Missing arrows showing direction.
Leaving out the antenna switch or PA.
examTips: A neat labelled diagram with functions earns full marks.
State the function of each block in one line.

practicals.title: Identifying electronic components on a phone board
practicals.aim: To identify surface-mount resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors, coils and ICs on a phone board and decode their markings.
safety: Use ESD protection.
procedure: View the board under magnification.
Identify SMD resistors (often black with code), capacitors (brown/tan, unmarked), coils, diodes, transistors and ICs (BGA and QFN packages).
Decode resistor codes.
Measure a removed resistor and compare.
Locate ICs by their location and markings (CPU, PMIC, charging IC, audio IC).
Tabulate findings.
practicals.expectedObservations: Most passive parts are tiny SMDs; ICs are BGA packages with balls underneath.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: SMD resistor codes: "103" = 10 × 10³ = 10 kΩ; "472" = 4.7 kΩ; "4R7" = 4.7 Ω (R marks the decimal point); "000" = 0 Ω link.
precautions: Do not lose tiny components; use tweezers over a tray.
sourcesOfError: Unmarked capacitors cannot be identified by value without measurement.
commonMistakes: Treating a 0 Ω link as faulty.
examTips: Name packages: SMD, BGA, QFN.
Decode resistor codes with working shown.

practicals.title: Continuity, short-circuit and voltage tests on a phone board
practicals.topic: Tracing and Fault Finding in Hardware
practicals.aim: To find faulty components by visual inspection, continuity and short-circuit tests, voltage measurement and current-draw analysis.
apparatus: DC power supply with current display
safety: Set the power supply current limit before connecting.
ESD protection.
procedure: Inspect the board for corrosion, burnt or missing parts.
Check the battery connector line for a short to ground (diode mode).
Connect the DC supply at battery voltage (e.g. 3.8 V) with current limit; press power and observe current.
Measure regulator output voltages at test points from the schematic.
Locate a shorted capacitor by feeling heat or using IPA evaporation when voltage is applied.
Replace the faulty component and retest.
practicals.expectedObservations: A dead short shows high current immediately with no power-on; a normal board draws a rising, fluctuating current as it boots.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Battery 3.7 V, 4 000 mAh stores 3.7 × 4.0 = 14.8 Wh. Charging at 2 A, charge time ≈ 4 000/2 000 × 1.2 = 2.4 h (allowing 20% for losses and tapering).
precautions: Begin with a low current limit.
Compare readings with a known good board.
sourcesOfError: Meter probes slipping on tiny pads.
commonMistakes: Applying full current to a shorted board (burns tracks).
examTips: Name methods: metering, signal tracing/injection, component testing, visual inspection.
Read PCB layouts and schematics to locate test points.

practicals.title: Replacing a damaged phone screen
practicals.aim: To remove a damaged display assembly and fit a replacement safely.

practicals.title: Replacing a charging port with hot-air rework
practicals.aim: To desolder and replace a faulty charging port or SMD component using a hot-air station.
safety: Shield nearby plastic parts with Kapton tape.
Use fume extraction; flux smoke is irritating.
procedure: Inspect the port for bent pins, dirt or broken joints.
Protect nearby parts with Kapton tape; apply flux.
Heat evenly with hot air (about 330–380 °C, moderate airflow) until solder melts; lift the port.
Clean pads with solder wick and IPA.
Apply flux and solder, place the new port and reflow.
Inspect joints for bridges under the microscope.
Test with the USB charging tester.
practicals.expectedObservations: The phone charges normally; the tester shows correct voltage and current.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Charger 5 V, 2 A gives a maximum of 5 × 2 = 10 W. The USB tester showing 5.05 V and 1.6 A means the phone is drawing 5.05 × 1.6 = 8.1 W.
precautions: Keep the hot-air nozzle moving to avoid burning the board.
Use enough flux.
sourcesOfError: Hidden pads under the connector not reflowed.
commonMistakes: Too high airflow blowing tiny parts away.
Not cleaning flux afterwards.
examTips: Define corrective maintenance and its procedures (cleaning, soldering, de-soldering, re-balling).
Describe the test after repair.

practicals.title: Preventive maintenance routine for a phone
practicals.aim: To carry out preventive maintenance: cleaning ports and contacts, checking battery health and updating software.
safety: Power off before cleaning ports.
Never use metal pins inside charging ports.
procedure: Back up the customer's data (with permission).
Clean the charging port, speaker grilles and SIM tray with brush and blower.
Wipe contacts with IPA.
Check battery health in settings or with a diagnostic app.
Check storage and remove unnecessary files (with permission).
Install software updates.
Record and advise the customer.
practicals.expectedObservations: Charging becomes reliable after removing lint; battery health and storage status are reported to the customer.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Battery design capacity 4 000 mAh; measured full-charge capacity 3 200 mAh. Health = 3 200/4 000 × 100 = 80%, the level at which replacement is often advised.
precautions: Use plastic, not metal, tools.
Back up before updating.
commonMistakes: Updating without backup or sufficient battery charge.
examTips: Define preventive maintenance and state its advantages.
List the procedures in order.

practicals.title: Using phone menus and codes for fault finding
practicals.aim: To use standard codes and phone menus to read the IMEI, check hardware through test menus and diagnose software faults.
safety: Never use codes that erase data without customer consent and backup.
procedure: Dial *#06# to display the IMEI and compare it with the label and box.
Verify the IMEI check digit (Luhn algorithm).
Open the manufacturer's test/diagnostic menu to test display, touch, speaker, microphone, vibrator and sensors.
Check SIM status and network settings in the menu.
Note symptoms: hanging, restart loops, SIM rejected.
Recommend a remedy (cache clear, update, reflash).
practicals.expectedObservations: The IMEI matches the label; the test menu identifies which hardware works.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Luhn check for IMEI 49015420323751_: double every second digit from the left (9, 1, 4, 0, 2, 7, 1 → 18, 2, 8, 0, 4, 14, 2; digits of 18 and 14 summed to 9 and 5), add all digits to get 52; check digit = (10 − 52 mod 10) mod 10 = 8. Full IMEI = 490154203237518.
precautions: Record settings before changing them.
sourcesOfError: Different makes use different test codes.
commonMistakes: Using unknown codes that reset the phone.
examTips: Explain software faults: SIM locked, SIM rejected, hanging, restart problem.
State the use of the IMEI.

practicals.title: Flashing firmware on a mobile phone
practicals.aim: To install (flash) official firmware to repair software faults such as boot loops, using the correct flashing tool.
apparatus: Computer with USB drivers and the maker's official flashing/repair tool
materials: Official firmware for the exact model
Customer consent and proof of ownership form
safety: Only flash phones with the owner's consent and proof of ownership; bypassing theft protection or changing IMEI is illegal.
Ensure at least 50% battery; never disconnect during flashing (can "brick" the phone).
procedure: Confirm the exact model number and region.
Back up user data if the phone is accessible.
Install drivers and the official tool on the computer.
Download the correct firmware and verify it.
Put the phone into download/recovery mode and connect.
Load the firmware and start flashing; wait until complete.
Reboot, complete setup with the owner's account and test.
practicals.expectedObservations: The phone boots normally after flashing; the boot loop is cleared.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Download time: a 2 GB firmware file at 10 Mbit/s takes 2 × 1 024 × 8/10 = 1 638 s ≈ 27 minutes.
precautions: Use only firmware for the exact model.
Use a stable power supply for the computer.
commonMistakes: Flashing wrong-region firmware.
Interrupting the process.
examTips: State the uses of flashing devices and software.
Mention the ethical and legal limits of unlocking.

practicals.title: Diagnosing SIM and network problems
practicals.aim: To diagnose and clear faults such as "Invalid SIM", "SIM card rejected", "Contact service provider" and phone lock code problems.
safety: Power off before removing the SIM tray.
procedure: Insert a known good SIM: if it works, the customer's SIM is faulty.
Inspect the SIM socket pins; clean and gently re-tension.
Check if the phone is network-locked (works only with one network).
Check settings: airplane mode, network mode, APN.
For "SIM card rejected", check the IMEI and network registration.
For a forgotten lock code, reset only with owner verification and their account credentials.
Record the cause and remedy.
practicals.expectedObservations: Most SIM errors are traced to a faulty SIM, dirty/bent socket pins, a network lock or settings.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Of 20 phones with SIM errors, 9 had faulty SIMs, 6 dirty or bent pins, 3 network locks and 2 software faults. Faulty SIMs = 9/20 × 100 = 45% of cases — so testing with a good SIM first saves time.
precautions: Test with a known good SIM before opening the phone.
commonMistakes: Reflashing before checking the SIM.
examTips: Give a step-by-step fault-finding sequence.
Explain service provider codes for checking balance and network services.

practicals.title: Testing chargers, batteries and accessories
practicals.aim: To identify phone accessories and test chargers, cables and batteries.
materials: Chargers, USB cables, power bank, earpiece/headset, Bluetooth headset, batteries
safety: Do not open mains chargers; they contain high voltages.
Do not short battery terminals.
procedure: Identify each accessory and state its function.
Measure the charger output voltage with no load.
Connect a phone through the USB tester and read voltage and current.
Test cables by swapping with a known good one and checking for voltage drop.
Measure a battery's open-circuit voltage.
Record and judge each item.
practicals.expectedObservations: A good charger holds about 5 V under load; a poor cable shows a larger voltage drop and lower current.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Charger 5.10 V at no load, 4.60 V while delivering 1.0 A through a cheap cable → drop = 0.50 V, so cable resistance ≈ 0.50/1.0 = 0.5 Ω. A good cable might drop only 0.15 V (0.15 Ω).
precautions: Use certified chargers.
commonMistakes: Judging a charger by its label alone.
examTips: State functions of headsets, earpiece, Bluetooth headset, batteries, chargers and cables.

practicals.title: Costing and return on investment for a phone repair shop
practicals.aim: To estimate the start-up cost of a phone repair workshop, its profit and return on investment, and identify risks.
materials: Survey sheet for shop rent, tools, equipment and parts prices
safety: Collect prices in pairs in safe market areas.
procedure: List capital items: tools, equipment, furniture, rent, registration.
Collect current prices and total the start-up capital.
Estimate monthly income from repairs and sales.
Estimate monthly expenses: rent, power, wages, parts.
Calculate monthly profit and return on investment.
List risks (theft, faulty parts, competition) and how to reduce them.
practicals.expectedObservations: A realistic budget shows how long it takes to recover the capital.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Start-up capital ₦1 200 000. Yearly income ₦3 000 000; yearly expenses ₦1 200 000 → yearly profit ₦1 800 000. ROI = 1 800 000/1 200 000 × 100 = 150%; payback time = 1 200 000/(1 800 000/12) = 8 months.
precautions: Use up-to-date local prices.
commonMistakes: Forgetting recurring costs such as power and rent.
examTips: State factors for choosing a shop location.
Show ROI formula and working.
